September 8, 2026

Report says senior DHS adviser Lewandowski sought Gulf state work and pressed Palantir

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Wall Street Journal reported that Corey Lewandowski, while serving as a senior adviser at the Department of Homeland Security under then-Secretary Kristi Noem, pitched wealthy Gulf states including Qatar and the United Arab Emirates on hiring him privately to help with matters under DHS jurisdiction, including visas. The report also says Lewandowski withheld signature on a $2.7 billion DHS agreement with Palantir while seeking a meeting with chief executive Alex Karp; Palantir officials cancelled the meeting and the contract was reduced to about $1 billion. Lewandowski is said to have been seeking a presidential pardon, which has not been granted.

Canadian retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of US goods take effect

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Canada's retaliatory tariffs have come into force, covering roughly $20 billion of US goods at rates from 15% to 50%. Products including milk, perfume, golf clubs, fishing rods, gaming consoles, jackets and t-shirts face tariffs of up to 50%, forklifts and industrial molds 15%, and cheese, carpets and certain household appliances 25%. Manufacturers in the Midwest are expected to be hit hardest. The measures took effect rather than being delayed or rolled back, as several US tariff announcements have been.

Glacier collapse in Nepal kills more than 1,300 as blame turns to fossil fuel companies

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

On August 26 a section of glacier broke off a mountain about 30 miles north of Kathmandu, sending rock, ice and mud into the Bhotekoshi River and producing a surge that registered as a 5.2 magnitude earthquake. The flood destroyed a hydro dam, dozens of bridges, the border crossing into Tibet and villages along the river, leaving more than 1,300 dead and nearly 5,000 missing. Warming is said to be softening the ice that binds high mountain rock together. A 2023 study in Science found that climate projections run by ExxonMobil's own scientists in the 1970s and 1980s largely matched what has since occurred, while the company publicly cast the science as unsettled; calls were made for restored disaster aid and USAID funding.

Iceland summons US ambassador over Trump annexation suggestion

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Iceland has summoned the United States ambassador and lodged a formal protest after President Trump suggested US control over Icelandic territory, with Reykjavik appearing on a map that also showed Mexico, Canada and parts of the Caribbean under US control. The Financial Times confirmed the ambassador was summoned and received the protest. Iceland relies on NATO for its defence, making the dispute a sensitive one between allies.

New York City releases 170,000 pages of 9/11 air quality records

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has released more than 170,000 pages of previously undisclosed records concerning air quality around ground zero after the September 11, 2001 attacks. The records indicate that officials knew the air was unsafe at the time and in the days afterward while publicly assuring residents it was safe to breathe. More than 49,000 people have since been diagnosed with World Trade Center-related cancers. Mamdani said people became ill because the leaders they trusted told them the air was safe.

Trump calls Iran conflict "small potatoes" as service member deaths mount

tags: politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

President Trump described the conflict with Iran as a military conflict rather than a war, saying it is "small potatoes for us" and "not a big thing," and referencing Venezuela in the same remarks. Eighteen US service members have died in the conflict. The characterisation drew criticism across the political spectrum for how it frames the loss of American lives.

Unaccompanied children face immigration court in Texas without lawyers as self-deportations rise

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

In immigration court in Harlingen, Texas, unaccompanied minors as young as four appear at proceedings without a lawyer or parent present. Sister Rose Patrice Kuhn, a 78-year-old Philadelphia nun who has worked in the Rio Grande Valley since 2022, attends Wednesday hearings, when children's cases are usually scheduled. She reports that a growing number of children and adults are telling judges they will self-deport — in 10 of 11 cases observed on one day — and that adults are increasingly being sent to third countries such as Ecuador or Uganda rather than their home countries, with judges saying their hands are tied.

Arctic lease sales fast-tracked next to Willow oil project

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Trump administration has mandated lease sales and is fast-tracking them without environmental review in the Fish Creek area of the Western Arctic, a 23 million-acre expanse that is the largest single piece of public land in the United States and an Iñupiat hunting and gathering ground. ConocoPhillips has already named the prospect twelve miles west of its Willow project "West Willow" and has drilled multiple exploration wells there. Roughly 75 million barrels are estimated to lie beneath the area, against global consumption of more than 100 million barrels a day. Campaigners are urging Congress to block the sales.

Russia seeks repayment of signing bonuses from convicted soldiers

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia is moving to reclaim part of the enlistment signing bonuses paid to soldiers who have since been convicted. The measure would require those service members to repay a portion of the money they received on joining.

Trump's Navy secretary pick needs congressional waiver to be confirmed

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Hung Cao, President Trump's pick to lead the Navy permanently, requires a congressional waiver before confirmation. Cao retired from active duty in 2021, and a seven-year rule bars recently serving officers from the post without legislative action.

Republican midterm convention in Dallas struggles to fill seats

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Organisers of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas are reportedly giving away free tickets after failing to attract enough attendees, according to the Daily Beast. Many Republican members of Congress have said they will not attend, citing the cost of attendance charged to members and concerns about the party brand. The event was scheduled against the opening night of the NFL season, and expected attendance is below the 2024 convention. Trump and the vice president are due to speak on Wednesday and Thursday nights.

House Republicans introduce bill to bar restaurant purchases with SNAP

tags: politics, health
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Representative Brandon Gill of Texas introduced the Ending Restaurant Purchases with SNAP Act of 2026 on September 3, arguing that recipients should not use benefits on fast food and junk food. Six Republican co-sponsors signed on: Randy Fine, Lauren Boebert, Keith Self, Barry Moore, Scott Perry and Ralph Norman. Critics note the bill would affect homeless and elderly recipients who lack the ability to cook. Only about one to three percent of bills introduced in the current Congress are enacted.

DHS to redesign seal so eagle faces the arrows, citing daily war footing

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The Department of Homeland Security announced changes to its seal to reflect that the department is, in its words, at war every single day, in a report published September 7. The current emblem shows an eagle holding an olive branch and a bundle of arrows, with its head turned toward the olive branch; Secretary Markwayne Mullin wants the head turned toward the arrows. Critics have drawn a comparison to the eagle emblems adopted by Nazi Germany, whose national emblem, decreed in 1935, faced the same direction as the proposed redesign.

Trump's account of being carried from a building near ground zero disputed

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump said two firefighters lifted him under the arms and carried him out of a building they believed was about to collapse in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks. The account refers to the US Steel building in Manhattan, not the World Trade Center, and there is no evidence he was inside during the period when the building was under structural concern. The claim drew criticism from 9/11 survivors and relatives of victims.

Clancy defence seeks presidential pardon as family lawyer threatens defamation action

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Attorney Kevin Reddington publicly asked President Trump to pardon Lindsay Clancy in appearances including Good Morning America. A federal pardon would not affect the state charges against her. A lawyer for Patrick Clancy issued a statement threatening legal action over what he called a relentless and escalating defamation campaign by influencers and conspiracy theorists claiming Patrick was involved in the deaths of his children. Prosecutors have not decided whether to retry Lindsay Clancy; the next hearing at the end of the month will address a Rule 25 motion and status issues.

Major base websites still list concealed carry bans five months after Hegseth order

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Five months after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued an order on firearms, the websites of several major military installations still state that concealed carry is banned on base. The discrepancy leaves official guidance to service members and visitors at odds with the department's directive.

Trump shares video whose news ticker highlights rising prices

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

As part of a Labor Day posting run on Truth Social, President Trump shared a video intended to show his administration holding companies accountable on prices. The news ticker visible in the clip carries figures including prices up 3.4% from a year earlier, food prices 3% higher than a year ago, a July consumer price index showing continued inflation, and a recall of nearly 30,000 pounds of Argentine beef imported into the United States. The post remained online.

USS Abraham Lincoln crew get first port call in 265 days

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln went ashore in Thailand for a few days after 265 days at sea without a port call, then returned to sea. The gap reflects the length of the carrier's current deployment.

Southern California beaches stripped of sand by severe erosion

tags: climate, environment
sources: @ericmoutsos

Stretches of beach in Southern California, including areas near San Diego, Carlsbad, Mission Beach and Balboa, have lost most or all of their sand. Footage shows sand levels dropped by roughly 20 feet in places, exposed rebar and steel, and sidewalks undermined along long sections of shoreline.
